diagnosis: The authoritative local daily-engine run run_daily-engine_pc-1786468021584 started at 2026-08-11T17:07:03Z and was externally reconciled as failed at 18:31:05Z after Windows Task Scheduler returned 0xC000013A and no process remained. The local platform log proves configuration deployment, Bakers capture, and Family Fare capture completed, then records START hy-vee-capture with no DONE, capture-ingest, native-publish, or ledger-finish; the existing Hy-Vee output predates this run, so the interrupted run published no partial capture or release. A power transition can therefore terminate the run with the observed status, but the Task Scheduler Operational channel is disabled, so battery stop versus a manual or other external stop cannot be proven retrospectively. Observability is additionally weak because scripts/run-pc-platform-job.ps1:36-43 buffers a child command's complete output before logging it, leaving no durable Hy-Vee progress after START. implementation: After the operator chooses the intended AC/battery policy, update platform/scripts/install-pc-platform-runtime.ps1:111-120 so Register-PcTask accepts an explicit power policy and the three-hour ThriftyCrew V3 Daily Engine task is registered with the selected, reviewable settings; if uninterrupted authoritative execution is selected, pass -AllowStartIfOnBatteries and -DontStopIfGoingOnBatteries instead of inheriting the current stop-on-battery defaults.

In platform/scripts/run-pc-platform-job.ps1:36-43, stream each child output line to Write-PcRuntimeLog while the child runs and preserve its native exit code, so the last completed Hy-Vee request/progress marker survives an external termination instead of leaving only START hy-vee-capture.

Add a read-only PC runtime verification script under platform/scripts that exports each registered V3 task and fails when its ExecutionTimeLimit, MultipleInstancesPolicy, or explicit power policy differs from repository authority; include the daily-engine 180-minute and chosen battery-policy assertions in the normal operator installation verification.

Do not retry, ingest, or publish from the interrupted workspace. A recovery must start a new fenced daily-engine run and reuse only immutable or independently validated inputs through the existing pipeline.

Terminate a second test child externally and prove its last progress line remains in the log for reconciliation.

Deployment check: run pnpm check, reinstall the PC runtime through the reviewed installer, export and inspect the registered Daily Engine task, then start one new fenced daily-engine recovery. Require config-deploy, all three captures, capture-ingest, browser-promotion, native-publish, Ghost reconciliation, direct parity, evidence accrual, and job-ledger-finish to log DONE before considering recovery complete.

Deployment check: confirm /api/v2/status reports the new daily-engine run completed, the current release changes only to a fully guarded immutable release, and /internal/doctor plus public API/board smoke checks pass. Preserve run_daily-engine_pc-1786468021584 and its evidence unchanged for audit.
rollback: If the selected power policy causes unacceptable battery drain, sleep interference, or duplicate scheduling, restore the prior explicit policy values and reinstall only the affected scheduled task; do not delete the durable failed run or its triage evidence.

If streamed logging changes exit-code propagation or leaks request payloads, revert the logging change, retain redaction at the existing operator boundary, and redeploy the previous launcher before the next scheduled run.

After rollback, export the task to prove its settings match the restored repository authority, confirm rel_native_cf4474d1e3965099cf85 or a later fully guarded release remains current, and leave daily-engine failed closed until a fresh complete run succeeds.
operatorReason: Task Scheduler history was disabled, so the evidence cannot distinguish a battery-triggered stop from a manual or other external termination. An operator must choose whether this three-hour local publisher is allowed to start and continue on battery, balancing continuity against battery drain, before the scheduler policy is changed.
